questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Courses relevant for my studies

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: not very intuitive. Lecture about housing being held, after all affordable housing had been filled/the deadline had passed. No introduction to exchange students about the practicalities until 1,2 weeks after arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not a lot. Again any assistance was given way after it was actually needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Assistance was available and very helpfull but only after arrival. Any assistance prior or any type of orientation was not available or only given after it was needed.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult as the housing lecture/help for housing was held after all affordable housing had been taken.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very expensive if the application is not early.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: would be nice to have on campus housing for exchange students, to form a relation between native and exchange students. And to reduce cost of living.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: very easy, but exchange students very "last" to pick, meaning that a lot of courses very filled. I had no personal trouble but I know a lot of people who couldn't get their requirements from their home institution met.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: an individual google application form for each course. Very easy to fill out and understand.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't now

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 3/4 courses, that I wanted. The last was unavailable for me due to waitlist.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have backups for your backups.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Bachelor courses are quite easy. I would recommend doing master courses along with bachelor courses. (400 = masters)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different, many powerpoints and "lectures" compared to practical and blackboard lectures at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Chemistry of environmental change (200 course), Applied quantum mechanics (400 course), Advanced materials chemistry (400 course), Polymer chemistry (400 course).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depends on their field. I would recommend Materials chemistry because the professor is very engaged and engaging.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Housing was way more expensive than I had planned more, because I hadn't been told I wasn't admitted to the dorm I had applied for, and assumed I had gotten, until very close to my moving date and by then all affordable options had been taken.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: all housing is expensive. Generally everything is expensive compared to DK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: almost everything. A lot of clubs and athletics.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Clubs or workout classes to make friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Local nature areas and trips to national parks.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: so-so. The work ethic is very different and the lecture times vary a lot. I had almost all my classes late in the evening which was very different.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs or be open in group works.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Very individualistic about their work. Not very likely to share/discuss answers or problems.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Friendlyness (outside of academics).

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Have backups for your courses. Find housing early, preferably with housemates/roommates. Go on trips and explore the country.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Your budget the first month is going to be about twice as big as your budget for the rest of the months.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Culture and personal development.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being on my own, both academically and personally.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
